q: Do the paper's 2D PEPS chapters (simple-update / full-update on Heisenberg or J1-J2) reproduce to comparable precision on a real problem, or does bond-dimension truncation dominate the physics at accessible D?
basis: This replication only exercised the 1D/MPS half of the notes; PEPS 2D benchmarks in Chap.~4 were left unrun because a laptop cannot fairly reach the D~7-10 regime needed. Whether the notes' pedagogical PEPS pipeline actually recovers, e.g., QMC-level Heisenberg energies at moderate D is an untested and highly load-bearing claim.
next_steps: Implement quimb.tensor PEPS simple-update on 2D Heisenberg at L=6, D=4..8; compare per-site energy to Sandvik QMC (published values). Free compute: uicgpu 8xA100 (Rick's small-batch free lane). Success = |E/N - E_QMC/N| < 5e-3 at D=8. Fallback: cite Corboz et al. 2014 PEPS benchmarks as external check.

q: Are the notes' contraction-complexity scaling claims (e.g., PEPS boundary-MPS O(chi^{10}), MERA O(chi^9)) empirically achievable, or does memory pressure change the effective exponent on modern hardware (GPU/TPU) with autodiff overhead?
basis: We accepted the paper's asymptotic-complexity statements without a single measured timing sweep. On modern GPUs the effective exponent can shift because of contraction-order heuristics, memory locality, and mixed-precision. This is a real open question for anyone using the notes as a practical guide today.
next_steps: Build a timing sweep script: fixed lattice, sweep chi in {8,16,24,32,48,64}, log wall-time on (a) CPU quimb, (b) GPU jax-based TN library (quimb + cotengra + jax), (c) A100. Fit log(t) vs log(chi) and compare slope to the paper's stated exponent. Free compute: uicgpu A100 idle. Deliverable: exponent + 95% CI per backend.

q: Do the notes' MPS/PEPS constructions extend cleanly to fermionic tensor networks (with swap gates or Grassmann tensors) without loss of the canonicalization / optimal-truncation guarantees the paper proves for the bosonic case?
basis: The paper discusses fermionic TNs only briefly. In particular, whether the C3 optimal-truncation theorem carries over to fermionic MPS in the presence of swap gates is not obviously true and was not tested here. This matters for any electronic-structure application of the notes.
next_steps: Take a fermionic Hubbard 1D chain at U=4, half-filling; run fermionic MPS (block2 or fMPS in quimb, if available) with canonical-form check; compare truncation error to sum_{k>chi} sigma_k^2 as we did for the bosonic case. Free compute: laptop or uicgpu. Deliverable: yes/no on whether the C3 identity still holds under fermion swap gates.

q: For the disordered / random-bond TFIM (still 1D, still MPS), does DMRG at fixed chi still recover the CFT-predicted entanglement scaling, or does infinite-randomness fixed-point physics (Refael-Moore c_eff = ln 2/6 * ln 2 flow) invalidate the clean-model chord-log fit the paper teaches?
basis: The paper's C2 pedagogy is illustrated on a clean critical Ising chain; whether the exact same MPS/entropy-fit workflow the notes teach still yields a meaningful 'c' in a disordered case is a natural next probe, and one that would tell the reader when the pedagogy breaks.
next_steps: Redo exp2 with h_i ~ Uniform(0.5, 1.5) (bond disorder) and average over 50 disorder realizations at N=64,128; fit slope; compare to Refael-Moore c_eff = (ln 2) * (ln 2 / 6) ~ 0.080 asymptote. Free compute: cherryrd CPU / uicgpu. Success = clear separation of clean vs disordered slope.

q: Do the notes' MPS/DMRG algorithms compose with modern autodiff (jax / pytorch) TN libraries such that variational optimization (e.g., of an ansatz's tensors against an energy target) recovers the same energies as the notes' fixed sweep-based DMRG?
basis: The notes predate the autodiff-TN wave. A reader following them today will likely use jax-based TN, where 'DMRG' becomes 'gradient descent on a variational MPS'. Whether the two approaches converge to the same energy at the same chi is unstated in the paper and untested here.
next_steps: Take the same TFIM N=32, chi=16 problem; run (a) our exp1 quimb DMRG, (b) a jax-autodiff MPS energy-minimizer (quimb + jax backend). Compare final E and #iterations for equivalent tolerance. Free compute: uicgpu A100. Deliverable: |E_DMRG - E_autodiff| and iteration-count ratio.
